findings.title: Legacy client profile allows cross-user invoice reads
findings.claim: The invoice handler resolves a per-request policy, and requests without a modern X-Client-Version fall into the legacy profile, under which the visibility check returns true without comparing invoice owners.

evidence.note: clientVersion returns null when X-Client-Version is missing, and isLegacyClient treats missing or old versions as legacy.
policyForRequest selects the legacy profile for such requests, and invoiceIsVisibleTo returns true for legacy without an ownership comparison.
handleInvoiceRead authenticates the caller and checks invoice existence, then enforces only that permissive visibility result before returning 200.

findings.validation: As Alice without X-Client-Version, request invoice-alice and invoice-bob. A 200 response containing owner bob for the second request confirms the authorization failure.

findings.title: Greeting page reflects names without escaping
findings.claim: The greet handler reads the name query parameter and interpolates it directly into the HTML response without calling the available escapeHtml helper.

evidence.note: escapeHtml exists and encodes markup characters, but no call site uses it.
greetName takes the raw query value and renderGreeting interpolates it into the page unescaped.
handleGreet serves the interpolated markup as text/html.

findings.validation: Request /greet with a markup name. A 200 response echoing the raw markup confirms the reflection.

findings.title: Docs reader follows parent-directory segments
findings.claim: The docs handler joins the file query parameter onto the docs root without a containment check, so parent-directory segments resolve outside the docs directory.

evidence.note: docsFilePath joins the raw parameter onto the docs root with no normalization or containment check.
isWithinRoot could reject escapes, but the handler never calls it.
handleDocs reads the joined path and serves its bytes with a 200 status.

findings.validation: Request /api/docs?file=../package.json. A 200 response with package metadata confirms the escape.
